clue.text: What's shot in Ambridge?

parts.note: Ambridge is the rural village of the long-running BBC radio soap The Archers, so what gets shot there is pheasant, partridge and the like on a country shoot

explanation.surface: A question about events in the fictional village of a radio soap opera.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the setting of The Archers, a BBC radio serial about country life; the question invites thoughts of a shooting in the plot, but the answer is the quarry of a country shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Pheasants and partridges are the quarry shot for sport in English villages, the kind of thing a shooting party bags.

clue.text: Woman's contribution to mass production

definitions.meaning: the ... in excelsis is a sung section of the Mass

explanation.surface: A woman's part in factory output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mass production' suggests factories but means a performance of the Mass.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a woman's name and the hymn of praise that forms part of the Mass setting.

clue.text: Prophet's work in a church in African country

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so these letters go within the country

parts.note: Mali is a country in West Africa

explanation.surface: A missionary's activity at a church in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' signals the container. 'Prophet's work' is a book of the Bible named after its prophet, the last of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: The last book of the Old Testament carries the name of the prophet it is attributed to.

clue.text: Loss of people's ability to benefit others

definitions.text: Loss of people's ability to benefit others

parts.words: Loss of people's ability to benefit others
parts.note: read as a decline in personal kindness, but meant as skilled, clever people leaving a country to work abroad

explanation.surface: A lament that people can no longer help one another.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ability' is meant as intellect, the talent a country loses when educated workers emigrate.
explanation.definitionFit: This phrase names the emigration of highly educated workers, whose skills then benefit other countries.

clue.text: Work with needle producing continuous pain in side

parts.note: running water is continuous, without break
a stitch is a sharp pain in the side, after running

explanation.surface: Sewing that gives a constant ache in the ribs.
explanation.definitionFit: A simple sewing technique in which the needle passes in and out in a continuous line.

clue.text: Reprimand backward section in private practice

indicators.note: backward says the hidden letters are read backwards
section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Telling off a doctor whose private clinic is slipping behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backward' turns the run TEPRAC found across 'private practice' ('section in') into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To carpet someone is an informal British verb for summoning them to be scolded, as if onto the boss's rug.

clue.text: Deserted by wife, cries and languishes

indicators.note: deserted by means left behind by, so that letter goes

parts.note: wails are cries

explanation.surface: Abandoned by his spouse, a man weeps and pines away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deserted by' removes W from WAILS.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who ails is unwell or feeble, which is what it means to languish.

clue.text: Leader of province with a mitre, possibly

definitions.text: Leader of province with a mitre, possibly

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
possibly suggests the letters might be put another way

explanation.surface: An archbishop described by his headgear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges A MITRE into RIMATE after the P that 'Leader of' takes from 'province'. The whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An archbishop presiding over an ecclesiastical province wears a mitre and holds that title.

clue.text: Time chap is in East, in Commonwealth state

indicators.note: is in means the chap is placed inside the region

parts.note: Asia is the East
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: A traveller spends a while in the Orient, in a Commonwealth country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is in' signals the container. 'Commonwealth' here is the Commonwealth of Australia, the country's formal name, not the wider group of nations.
explanation.definitionFit: Tasmania is one of the six states of the Commonwealth of Australia.

clue.text: Bird of prey taking lead from tame one

indicators.note: taking the lead away from a word means its first letter is removed

parts.note: a fowl is a domesticated bird, the tame kind kept in a farmyard

explanation.surface: A hawk or eagle picking up tips from a domestic bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking lead from' removes F, the first letter of FOWL.
explanation.definitionFit: Owls are nocturnal raptors that hunt mice and voles, so they count as birds that prey on others.

clue.text: 'Angs around with friends, targets for criticism

parts.note: hangs around means haunts; the apostrophe drops the H as a Cockney would, giving the dropped-aitch form
allies are friends or supporters

explanation.surface: Someone loiters with pals, picking people out to pick on.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe on 'Angs signals the Cockney dropped H, so the synonym for hangs around loses its H too. An Aunt Sally is a fairground game of throwing sticks at a dummy's head.
explanation.definitionFit: From the fairground throwing game, an Aunt Sally is a person or idea set up to be attacked, a ready target.

clue.text: From nine to five, perhaps, seen in a suit? Don't bet against it!

definitions.text: From nine to five, perhaps, seen in a suit? Don't bet against it!

parts.words: From nine to five, perhaps, seen in a suit? Don't bet against it!
parts.note: read as office hours in business dress, but meant as a poker hand of five cards in sequence, all of one suit

explanation.surface: An office worker in formal wear on a safe bet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nine to five' suggests a working day, but it describes card values; 'suit' is hearts or spades, not business clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker, five consecutive cards of the same suit form one of the strongest hands, almost unbeatable.

clue.text: Awfully nice new record getting people excited

indicators.note: awfully suggests the word nice is badly mangled into a new order

parts.note: a diary is a daily record

explanation.surface: A dreadful new album that stirs up a crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' is the anagram signal on 'nice', giving INCE; 'record' is a diary, not a disc, despite the musical surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Incendiary speech is inflammatory, firing people up the way an incendiary device starts a blaze.

clue.text: Darling dog of Zola's heroine

definitions.meaning: in Peter Pan the Darling family's nursemaid is a Newfoundland dog
Emile Zola's 1880 novel is named after its courtesan heroine

explanation.surface: A pet hound belonging to the leading lady of a French novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Darling' looks like an endearment, but it is the surname of the children's family in Peter Pan.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the Darlings' Newfoundland nurse in Barrie's play and the title courtesan of Zola's novel carry this name.

clue.text: One may join in Rule Britannia and Emperor waltz

definitions.text: One may join in Rule Britannia

indicators.note: waltz suggests the letters whirling round into a new order

explanation.surface: Concert music: patriotic song and a Strauss waltz.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waltz' rearranges AND EMPEROR. The Emperor Waltz is by Strauss. Rule Britannia is sung by the audience at London's Last Night of the Proms concert.
explanation.definitionFit: A concertgoer at the BBC Proms, who sings along to Rule Britannia on the last night.

clue.text: Crude producer repelled lassie I love

indicators.note: repelled means driven back, so the string is read backwards

parts.note: a lassie is a Scottish girl
love is zero in tennis, written as O

explanation.surface: A rough-mannered man is rebuffed by a girl he declares his love for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repelled' turns GIRL + I + O into the answer. 'Crude' is oil, not rude.
explanation.definitionFit: An offshore drilling platform pumps crude oil out of the seabed, making it a producer of crude.

clue.text: As national of modern republic, is one welcoming king's reverse?

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in a guest, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: taken as written
one is I, the Roman numeral

indicators.note: reverse means the king's name is read backwards

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: Asking whether a citizen of a young state is someone who welcomes a monarch's defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' turns the king to RAEL, and 'welcoming' houses it; 'reverse' looks like a setback for a monarch, and 'As' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A citizen of the state of Israel, founded in 1948, is a national of a modern republic.

clue.text: Strong criticism one of us holds back, oddly

indicators.note: holds means contains, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: the Times is a British paper, so one of us is a Brit

indicators.note: oddly suggests the letters are arranged strangely

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: One of our group strangely keeps silent about a harsh review.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' is an anagram signal giving CKBA, not a call for odd letters; 'holds' signals the container. 'one of us' assumes British readers of The Times.
explanation.definitionFit: A brickbat is literally a piece of brick thrown as a missile, figuratively a harsh critical remark.

clue.text: Traveller isn't commonly required to put on another coat

parts.note: a commercial traveller is a sales rep
ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A salesman doesn't have to wear an extra layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests clothing but means a layer of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint is to apply a fresh layer of paint over the old one.

clue.text: Arrogant youngster staying about two seconds for exercise

indicators.note: a stay holds things in place, so the youngster contains the rest

parts.note: a pup is a cheeky or conceited young man
RE means about or concerning
S is the abbreviation for second, twice

explanation.surface: A cocky young man lingers a couple of moments before working out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'staying' signals the container, as a stay holds something in. Press-ups are what Americans call push-ups.
explanation.definitionFit: A press-up, called a push-up in the US, is a floor exercise raising the body on the arms.

clue.text: In accepting silver, showing respect

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: being in means being at home
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: Receiving a silver trophy with deference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a link word but gives HOME, as in 'stay in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Homage is public honour or deference paid to someone, an act of showing esteem.

clue.text: Prize for one who played Dorothy

definitions.meaning: a wreath of flowers awarded as an honour
Judy, the actress who starred as Dorothy in The Wizard of Oz

explanation.surface: An award for the actress in The Wizard of Oz.
explanation.definitionFit: A wreath given as an honour, and the surname of the actress Judy who played Dorothy in 1939.

clue.text: Yank wearing jacket

parts.note: to yank is to jerk
in means wearing, as in dressed in

explanation.surface: An American in a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yank' looks like an American but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A jerkin is a close-fitting sleeveless jacket, often leather.

clue.text: Provided a wake-up call for those on board

definitions.meaning: a cockerel provides a wake-up call when it crows, and an old past tense of crow is this word
the people working on a ship

explanation.surface: Someone rang the cabin early to rouse the passengers.
explanation.walkthrough: The old past tense of 'crow', as in 'the cock crew', is the first sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's company, the people working aboard, and the archaic past tense of a cockerel crowing.

clue.text: Fish with rod in tender, helping sister

parts.note: a staff is a rod or stick
the nurse shark and nursehound are fish

explanation.surface: Fishing with a rod from a small boat, lending a hand to one's sister.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tender' looks like a boat but is someone who tends. A sister is a senior ward nurse in British hospitals; the answer is the grade below.
explanation.definitionFit: In British hospitals this grade of nurse tends patients and works under the ward sister.

clue.text: Emperor in love, having head turned

indicators.note: the first letter is rotated on its side, which turns one letter shape into another

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring

explanation.surface: A Roman ruler in love looks back over his shoulder.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having head turned' rotates the first letter of ZERO by a quarter turn, and a Z on its side looks like N.
explanation.definitionFit: Nero was the Roman emperor said to have fiddled while Rome burned.

clue.text: Sure to include positive quality, hard to find in this breed

indicators.note: to include means to take in, so one piece holds the others

parts.note: being bound to do something means being sure to
an asset is a useful quality
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A dog breed whose good traits are said to be elusive.
explanation.definitionFit: This short-legged long-eared scent hound is a recognised dog breed.

clue.text: Bird Cockney might misidentify from sound

definitions.text: Bird Cockney might misidentify from sound

parts.words: Bird Cockney might misidentify from sound
parts.note: a Londoner who drops initial H would say the name of a bird of prey in a way that matches a seabird's name

explanation.surface: A Londoner mistaking one bird for another by its call.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys famously drop their aitches, so a hawk comes out as 'awk.
explanation.definitionFit: The auk is a seabird whose name matches the dropped-aitch Cockney way of saying hawk.

clue.text: Excellent spinner following gratuitous advice?

indicators.note: following means coming after, so this piece goes second

parts.note: a tip is a piece of advice and also a gratuity, hence advice that is gratuitous
a top is a spinning toy

explanation.surface: A great bowler responding to unsolicited coaching.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinner' suggests a cricket bowler but is the toy.
explanation.definitionFit: Tip-top is an informal British adjective for first-rate or splendid.

clue.text: Irish writer, in general, esteemed by Americans

definitions.meaning: Richard Brinsley the playwright, born in Dublin, wrote The Rivals
Philip Henry the Union cavalry general of the US Civil War is a national hero

explanation.surface: A Dublin author held in high regard by readers across the Atlantic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in general' reads as 'generally', but 'general' is a military rank.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the Dublin playwright of The School for Scandal and to a celebrated Union general.
